newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DENNIS MARTINEZ ANNOUNCES HIS RETIREMENT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DENNIS MARTINEZ ANNOUNCES HIS RETIREMENT.

text.p: Right-hander Dennis Martinez, just two wins short of becoming the Latin American pitcher with the most victories ever in the major leagues, announced his retirement on Wednesday.

The 42-year-old Martinez was released on May 24 by the Seattle Mariners. The native Nicaraguan finishes his career with a 241-187 record, a pair of wins shy of Hall of Famer Juan Marichal's total of 243.

"After playing major league baseball for 21 seasons, I have come to the conclusion that it is now time to leave the game," said Martinez in a statement released by the Major League Players Association.
"I have been blessed many times in my life, but after my family, I view my career in baseball as the greatest blessing of all."
Nicknamed "El Presidente," he is one of only seven pitchers in history to win 100 games in both leagues.
Martinez was ineffective in nine starts with Seattle this season, going 1-5 with a 7.71 ERA. In 49 innings, he surrendered 65 hits, including eight home runs.
The right-hander broke into the big leagues with Baltimore in 1976 and pitched with the Orioles for 11 seasons, battling an alcohol problem along the way.

He was dealt to Montreal in June 1986 and enjoyed a resurgence in eight seasons with the Expos, tossing a perfect game -- the 15th in major league history -- against the Dodgers in Los Angeles in 1991.
After appearing on three All-Star teams and leading the majors with a 2.39 ERA in 1991, he signed as a free agent with Cleveland in 1994 and helped them reach the World Series in 1995.

Martinez was limited to 20 starts with the Indians last year due to right elbow problems, but went 9-6 with a shutout and a 4.50 ERA. The nine wins snapped his nine-year streak of double-figure victories.
"I've had the chance to play with some of the best baseball players ever," added Martinez. "I want to thank my fellow teammates for always being there for me. I've had a wonderful career."
